content:
Yesterday we saw three fearful judgments in Numbers 16. The earth opened and swallowed the rebels. Fire came from God and consumed the two hundred and fifty men. And finally a plague entered the congregation, and fourteen thousand seven hundred died. We must remember that Yahweh's fatherhood does not cancel His holiness. He disciplines His people, and the New Creation is therefore called to repent early, rather than to harden the heart. Today let us begin to turn these judgments into warnings for ourselves, for these three judgments can become three very serious warnings for the New Creation.

We should not say that God will literally open the earth, send visible fire, or send a plague every time a believer sins. Rather, the principles behind these judgments show us what rebellion can do to our spiritual life. Today we will consider the first two, the earth and the fire, and we will keep the third for tomorrow.

First there is the earth, and it teaches us that rebellion can swallow our spiritual life. Korah, Dathan, and Abiram rose against the authority Yahweh had established. They were not satisfied with the position Yahweh had given them. Korah wanted what had not been assigned to him, while Dathan and Abiram openly refused Moses' authority. Then the earth opened beneath the rebels and swallowed them (Numbers 16:31-33). For the New Creation there is a powerful warning here: when we reject Yahweh's order because we want our own way, earthly things can begin to swallow our spiritual life. Paul says, "Set your mind on things above, not on things on the earth" (Colossians 3:2).

Think of a brother who once loved prayer, Scripture, and fellowship. Then his career begins to prosper. Slowly his whole mind becomes occupied with salary, promotion, property, and recognition. He does not necessarily deny Christ with his mouth. But prayer becomes few seconds, Scripture becomes occasional, and fellowship becomes inconvenient, while his earthly ambitions consume his thoughts. The earth has begun to swallow him. Or imagine a sister who receives correction in the fellowship. Instead of examining herself, she thinks, "Why should they tell me what to do? I know just as much as they do." Pride grows. Then she finds two people who agree with her. Soon they are privately discussing the faults of others. What began as an unwillingness to receive correction becomes bitterness, division, and eventually separation.

That resembles Korah's road. We have already seen that jealousy can lead to rebellion when we resist the assignment Yahweh has given us, while Scripture says that God has placed the members in the body "as it hath pleased Him"(1 Corinthians 12:18). The warning of the earth is therefore this: do not allow earthly ambition, pride, jealousy, position, money, offence, or self-will to swallow the New Creation.

Then there is the fire, and it teaches us not to treat holy things as common. The second judgment was different from the first. The two hundred and fifty men came with censers and attempted to offer incense before Yahweh.They were approaching a holy service according to their own claim, rather than according to Yahweh's appointment. Then, the Scripture says, "Fire came out from God and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering incense" (Numbers 16:35). For the New Creation, this warns us about presumption in holy things. We can begin to think, "I am baptized. I know the Truth. I attend fellowship. I know the doctrines. Therefore I can live however I want." But knowledge of holy things does not give us permission to treat them casually. A very strong New Testament warning says that a far worse punishment belongs to the one "who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, counted the blood of the covenant... a common thing" (Hebrews 10:29).

Consider a practical example. A believer knows that something is sinful.
His conscience warns him. Scripture has already corrected him. Yet he deliberately continues, and tells himself, "Christ died for me anyway. God will forgive me." That is very different from a believer who falls through weakness, becomes broken over the sin, confesses it, and seeks cleansing. The dangerous attitude says, "I know it is wrong, but I will do it anyway, because grace will cover me." Paul directly rejects such thinking, "Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? Certainly not!" (Romans 6:1-2). The two hundred and fifty men held something holy in their hands while their hearts were standing in rebellion. And we too can hold a Bible in our hands, take the bread and the cup, sing hymns, preach, pray publicly, attend meetings, and speak about Christ, and yet secretly permit pride, immorality, hatred, jealousy, or deliberate disobedience in the heart. The warning of the fire is therefore this: never become familiar with holy things while losing holy fear.

So the earth warns us not to let earthly things swallow our devotion, and the fire warns us not to treat holy things as common. But there was a third judgment in Numbers 16, and in some ways it is the most frightening of all.

For it did not fall upon the rebels who had started the trouble, nor upon the two hundred and fifty who had seized the censers. It fell upon the ordinary congregation, the watching crowd, the very people who had just seen the earth open and the fire fall with their own eyes. How could judgment come upon those who had witnessed such things? What had they done, only a day later, to bring a plague into the camp? And where, in the middle of that plague, did mercy suddenly appear? That is where we will continue tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God, holy and gracious, who disciplines the people You love,
Do not let earthly ambition, pride, or offence swallow up our spiritual life.

Set our minds on things above, and keep us content with the place You have given us.

Guard us from ever handling holy things while our hearts stand in rebellion.

Let us never grow so familiar with sacred things that we lose our holy fear of You.

Keep us from saying, 'I will sin, for grace will cover me,' and make us quick to repent.

"Set your mind on things above, not on things on the earth." - Colossians 3:2

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
